questions.markdown:
The area of a circle $(A)$ corresponding diameter $(D)$ is given below.

| $D$ | 80 | 85 | 90 | 95 | 100 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| $A$ | 5026 | 5674 | 6362 | 7088 | 7854 |

Find the area corresponding to diameter 105 using Newton's interpolation method.

questions.markdown:
The following data were collected when a large oil tanker was loading. Calculate the flow rate at time $t = 20$ mins.

| $t$ (mins) | 0 | 10 | 20 | 30 | 40 | 50 | 60 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| $V$ ($10^6$ barrels) | 0.4 | 0.7 | 0.77 | 0.88 | 1.05 | 1.17 | 1.35 |

Also compute

$$
\frac{d^2V}{dt^2}
$$

at $t = 60$ mins. Here, $V$ is the volume of the oil present in the tank at time $t$.

diagrams.caption: Data table of time t and oil volume V (original source region)

questions.markdown:
Using Runge Kutta method of fourth order, solve

$$
\frac{dy}{dx} = 3x + \frac{y}{2}, \quad y(0)=1
$$

for $y(0.2)$ taking $h = 0.1$.

The velocity $v$ of a particle at distance $s$ from a point on its path is given by the table:

| $s$ ft. | 0 | 10 | 20 | 30 | 40 | 50 | 60 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| $v$ ft./sec. | 47 | 58 | 64 | 65 | 61 | 52 | 38 |

Estimate the time taken to travel 60 ft by using Simpson's $1/3$rd rule.

diagrams.caption: Data table of distance s and velocity v (original source region)

questions.markdown:
Using Gauss Seidel method solve the system of equations

$$
2x + y + 6z = 9; \quad 8x + 3y + 2z = 13; \quad x + 5y + z = 7.
$$

Carry out 4 iterations correct up to 4 decimal places.

Solve

$$
\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} - \frac{dy}{dx} - 2y = e^{(e^x+3x)}
$$

by the method of variation of parameters.

Find the root of the equation

$$
f(x) = \cos x - xe^x = 0
$$

which lies between 0 and 1 by the Regula Falsi method. Carryout 4 iterations.

questions.markdown: Using Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization process construct an orthonormal set of vectors from the set of $\{(1,1,1), (-1,0,-1), (-1,2,3)\}$ for $\mathbb{R}^3$.

$$
A = \begin{bmatrix}2 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 2\end{bmatrix}
$$

By Rayleigh-Power method by taking the initial vector as $[1,0,0]^T$
Define the basis of a vector space. Prove that in a vector space $V$ over a field $F$, every maximal linearly independent set of vectors forms a basis for $V$.

Consider the initial value problem $y' = x(y + 1), y(0) = 1$.
Compute $y(0.2)$ with $h = 0.1$ using Taylor series method.
Consider up to the fourth order term.

Using Gauss-Jordan method, find the inverse of

$$
A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 2 & -1 & 3 \\ 4 & 1 & 8\end{bmatrix}.
$$
